evidence.mission_note: A manual 3.0i roadster in the ideal price band fits the enthusiast-bridge brief directly. Its bridge value depends on proving the undocumented areas: structure, cooling and the deer-strike repair.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2001 Z3 3.0i roadster with a factory manual, shown in photos with a stock-looking engine bay and well-kept beige interior, asking $14,500, just below the $15,058 fair-value mid. Observed issues are a disclosed deer strike with hood replacement and no repair paperwork, a thumb-sized rear-quarter dent, a torn trunk liner, and an expansion tank that appears aged and discoloured. Mileage is given as both 28,000 and 27,000, and the rear plate tab appears to read 01/22, so the photos may be several years old. There is no VIN, no title statement and no service receipts. Both model-critical items, rear subframe/trunk-floor condition and cooling-system history, are unproven. The tracker also links this vehicle to a 78,000-mile listing without a VIN; that is more likely a mis-link than an odometer issue, but only a VIN and history report can settle it.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a current odometer photo, and photos under the trunk carpet; then run a Carfax/AutoCheck to confirm title and mileage trail before arranging a Twin Cities BMW-specialist PPI.
